symptom: `check -p` printed "no flow change exec would refuse" (and exec's preflight said nothing) for a script whose `create or modify microflow` exec then refused with MDL-V1-REBUILD ("replace $X: $X is still used by") — after writing the statements before it. The trigger: the new body calls a flow an earlier statement of the same script creates
cause: CheckFlowVerdicts builds the declared flow against the stored project and skips any flow whose build fails as "not predictable"; a CALL MICROFLOW to a flow the script creates earlier fails microflowExists ("not found in the project"), so the verdict was silently skipped and the check line claimed full coverage
file: mdl/executor/validate_flow_verdicts.go (checkFlowVerdicts, flowModifyViolations), mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder.go (declaredFlow/scriptFlows overlay), cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go, cmd/mxcli/exec_preflight.go
insight: A check-time prediction that skips what it cannot build must say so: a silent skip reads as a pass, and the skip set is exactly the multi-statement scripts where a half-applied exec hurts. Fix is an overlay of the script's own CREATE [OR MODIFY] MICROFLOW|NANOFLOW signatures in the builder (generalising the self-call `selfFlow` of #843), plus an Unpredicted list (FormatUnpredictedFlows) for whatever still does not build. Revert proof: stub the overlay lookup and the multi-statement case reports no violation, only the unpredicted note
